In reality, the speed of sound ($v$) is a property of the medium, determined by its elasticity and density (which relates to the distance between molecules). The relationship $v = f\lambda$ implies that if the speed is fixed by the medium, the wavelength ($\lambda$) must change to accommodate a constant frequency ($f$); thus, wavelength is a *result* of the speed, not the *cause*.
